findings.status: New conditional source arithmetic finding; supported program reachability, policy and exact alias remain unresolved
findings.condition: A parent candidate passes the selector condition recipient_y + 0.08 < source_low and produces the ParentRoofFace disposition. For actual computed f32 values the eventual reconstructed outlet-void centre is at or below (recipient_y + 0.06) + 0.08. This includes a real-arithmetic gap strictly between 0.08 and 0.21 metres when rounding is small; endpoints and large-coordinate precision require separate qualification. The station/network must reach the corresponding roof audit to obtain the stated audit issue.
findings.observation: Selection accepts any parent more than 0.08 m below source_low, but the emitted outlet is source_low − 0.07 m and the discharge is recipient_y + 0.06 m. The audit requires reconstructed outlet centre > discharge + 0.08 m. Therefore the stated source-level interval can be selected yet fails fall_is_vertical, making that station invalid in the roof drainage check. The document path calls audit_plan and rejects issues, while generate directly calls generate_unchecked; no unsupported plan or emitted runtime instance has been demonstrated.
findings.historical_relation: Related to 059 L12-CLOSURE-ROOF-OUTLET-FALLBACK-ACCEPTANCE and native NATIVE-ROOF-PPS-TRACE-016, but those records inventory fallback and require final audit proof; the selected-parent height gap is a different precise predicate and no automatic alias or accepted count is claimed. Reconcile with any existing drainage acceptance owner centrally.
findings.future_direction: Establish admitted parent/child gap and intended fall geometry. If supported, align candidate admission, authored offsets and the final audited fall contract; preserve valid parent and ground dispositions and source error policy.

findings.status: Current conditional continuation of 059 READ-L12-864 topology question; independent acceptance and actual supported nonconvex topology remain open
findings.condition: A finite nondegenerate face or cutout permits a fixed 5×5 grid midpoint which the intended general weather-face containment classifies differently from the all-edge convex predicate, with equal nonzero signed-area orientations in both computations. The strongest vacuous case additionally has no expected midpoint under the convex predicate and an existing network with zero samples.
findings.observation: RoofPlanSampling projects a face and each cutout then applies an all-edge half-plane test to the 25 grid centres. The roof drainage audit independently recomputes a 5×5 grid and the same orientation/all-edge predicate with the same side threshold. It therefore does not independently restore a grid point omitted by that same predicate. If expected and retained sample sets are empty, sample validity and coverage checks use all() over empty collections and count equality; those sample checks can pass if all other channel/station requirements pass. The separate weather recipient uses a general even/odd polygon query. Current child-cut construction takes a convex hull before storing those particular cutouts, which narrows rather than proves the topology question.

findings.future_direction: Establish what face/cutout topology is actually admitted and whether empty sampling is valid. If general nonconvex topology is supported, use an appropriate containment contract and independent coverage check while preserving numerical tolerance and accepted cutout behavior.

findings.status: Conditional current source observation; alternative availability, obstacle case and required prioritization are unproved
findings.condition: The nearest obstacle-clear first-pass parent-face candidate is not below source_low by the required 0.08 m, while another first-pass candidate is sufficiently lower and obstacle-clear. The later cardinal fallback encounters a different lower contained face first whose fall is blocked.
findings.observation: The first pass ranks all obstacle-clear contained candidate/face pairs by plan distance before testing the winning face’s height. If that winner is too high, it does not try the next obstacle-clear candidate; it switches to fallback, which tests containment and height but not obstacle clearance. The later roof audit can reject a resulting fall under its own collision criteria, whereas the source generator has already selected the fallback. The stated combination is a reasoning condition, not a demonstrated generated layout.
findings.historical_relation: Connected to 059 L12-CLOSURE-ROOF-OUTLET-FALLBACK-ACCEPTANCE, but that prior record asks whether fallback is accepted and does not prove this candidate-selection ordering. findings.future_direction: Determine supported overlapping parent face topology and intended preference ordering; if the condition is supported, consider selecting among candidates that satisfy both clearance and height before any explicitly qualified fallback.

findings.condition: No candidate passes the source filter and the last candidate is chosen, then a retained network reaches the roof audit. Where that candidate fails the audit’s own clearance, vertical fall, roof intersection, portal or stair predicates, station validity fails; the audit is not identical to the full generator search.
findings.observation: The source generator selects the last enumerated candidate on an exhausted search. The roof audit checks station fall clearance and disposition, and document generation rejects any issues. The plain generate function does not invoke that audit. These facts do not establish that all rejected source candidates fail every downstream audit or that any supported layout reaches fallback.

Can a nearer high obstacle-clear face and a farther lower clear face coexist, and should source selection exhaust all clear candidates before geometric fallback?
What polygon and cutout topology is admitted for every producer, and is a zero-sample drainage network acceptable? Can a grid point inside a supported nonconvex face be removed by the convex test?
Do separate independent roof/timber audit and editor acceptance reject every meaningful blocked fallback, including collector-only failures? Plain generate bypasses audit.
What is the intended station cap for gable/hip roofs, and can supported geometry actually produce more than two?
Can admitted walls shorter than 0.24 m reach either f32 clamp with ordered finite bounds; is a prior error boundary guaranteed?
Can any station contain more than 32 generated networks, and are ID namespace and recipients unique across all producers?
Is consolidation eligible to repeat on retained geometry? It clears stations but appends recipient surfaces and collectors and extends catchment state; actual lifecycle and cleanup are unproven.

How should route, station, recipient and topology owners express their aggregate invariants without conflating the already recorded 0x6000 junction collision, 0x7800 collector domain, and 774 checked-position producer propagation?

lenses.assessment: No domain String API in assigned bodies; diagnostic expect labels are not string-based control flow. Closed drainage modes and structured source errors remain distinct.

Cap4, side tolerance 0.002, 5×5 sampling, fall offsets, clearances and packed-ID masks encode different policy/units; named ownership and numerical error budgets require further reconciliation rather than one generic constant.
RoofDrainageDisposition and Recipient are owned enums and IDs are typed, while outlet/station/face payload ownership and global ResolvedItemId namespace are the actual cross-owner questions.

SpatialBounds and CollisionCuboid carry admitted architectural values while plan/height/normal values and sampled state remain raw; consult existing canonical geometric types before creating replacements.
A station has independent disposition, optional host/downspout and recipient; only a supported aggregate contract justifies re-shaping it, not the mere presence of Option or a native index.
Parent gap arithmetic combines three different offsets; clamp ordering, normal denominator, near-zero projection and repeated geometry edits need operation-specific proofs.

A network, station, edge, catchment, route, outlet, recipient surface, spout and disposition must agree. The roof audit checks many associations but does not by itself establish all admission and lifecycle guarantees.
The parent selector admits a weaker height gap than the independent audited minimum; actual supported gap remains open. Local nonempty chunk/offset invariants are established by control flow.

Three dispositions and two recipient variants retain named roles, while their accompanying optional fields require supported combinations; do not infer a failure solely from enum/Option representation.

Sampler and drainage audit each recompute the same convex 5×5 coverage, and station/network/catchment/route retain related IDs. Repeated state or a duplicated numerical predicate is not sufficient alone to claim unintended independent authority.

Preserve ordering, station grouping, host/free-drip/ground modes, deterministic offset candidates, native errors and checked-document versus plain-generation boundaries unless product policy deliberately changes.
